'''Gregory Darnell Smith''' (born January 28, 1947) is an American former [[basketball]] player. He was a starter on the 1970–71 [[Milwaukee Bucks]] [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) championship team.

== Early life ==
Smith was born on January 28, 1947, in [[Princeton, Kentucky]], the son of Henry and Pearl (Hill) Smith.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-2">{{Cite web |title=Greg Smith Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smithgr01.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2008-01-22 |title=Henry Smith, 83 |url=https://www.timesleader.net/obituaries/henry-smith-83/article_ed6aec6b-fd8f-5a04-95ca-dd899b93439c.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=The Times Leader |language=en}}</ref> He attended Dotson High School in [[Caldwell County, Kentucky]], which later merged with Caldwell County High School. Smith played on Dotson's basketball team with his older brother [[Dwight Smith (basketball)|Dwight]].<ref name="Steger-1996">{{Cite news |last=Steger |first=Sam |date=November 6, 1996 |title=Dotson High achieved basketball fame |work=Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky) |pages=32}}</ref> He graduated from Caldwell County High in 1964.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-1982">{{Cite news |date=April 8, 1982 |title=Greg Smith praised for his ability on team that won NBA crown |work=The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky) |pages=11}}</ref> His Dotson teams won district titles in the 1961–62 and 1962–63 seasons, and he was named to the district  All-Tournament teams.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000">{{Cite news |date=June 28, 2000 |title=Chamber recruits Greg Smith to speak at annual banquet |work=The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky) |pages=A1–A2}}</ref> Greg and Dwight twice led their Dotson team to the Kentucky state basketball tournament.<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" /> Smith was named to the Second Region All-Tournament Team in 1962–63.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" />

As a senior (1963–64) at Caldwell County High, the team's won–loss record was 24–7. Smith averaged 16.1 points per game, and established its single game [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounding]] record with 37 (21 offensive). He was again named to the district All-Tournament Team; with Caldwell winning the district title. In 1964, he was again named to the Second Region All-Tournament Team, and was named that tournament's Most Valuable Player. Caldwell reached the quarterfinals of the Kentucky State High School Championship Tournament, with Smith making the All-State Tournament Team as well.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" />

He is the only Caldwell County High player to have his jersey number retired.<ref name="Kentucky High School Basketball Hall Of Fame-2023">{{Cite web |last= |date=2023-05-31 |title=Greg Smith, Kentucky High School Basketball Hall of Fame |url=https://khsbhf.com/greg-smith/ |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Kentucky High School Basketball Hall Of Fame |language=en-US}}</ref>

== College ==
Smith followed his brother Dwight to attend [[Western Kentucky University]] on a basketball scholarship, where he majored in physical education and social work.<ref name="Steger-1996" /><ref name="Engelhardt-1988">{{Cite news |last=Engelhardt |first=Gordon |date=March 13, 1988 |title=Greg Smith's aggressiveness helped him land a radio job |work=The Sunday Courier (Evansville, Illinois) |pages=32}}</ref><ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" /> He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball|Western Kentucky Hilltoppers]]. As a sophomore (1965–66), Smith averaged 9.5 [[Points per game|points]] and 10.3 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds per game]] (8th best in the conference).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Greg Smith College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/greg-smith-14.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1965–66 Men's Ohio Valley Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/ovc/men/1966.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The [[1965–66 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|Hilltoppers]] were the 1966 [[Ohio Valley Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Ohio Valley Conference]] champions.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Beavers |first=Danny |date=February 24, 1966 |title=Western Clinches OVC Champ Roll |work=Caldwell County Times (Princeton, Kentucky) |pages=15}}</ref>

The team had a 25–3 record and ranked 10th in the final [[Associated Press]] (AP) college basketball poll among men's Division I teams.<ref name="College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com">{{Cite web |title=1965–66 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Men's Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/western-kentucky/men/1966.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> His teammates included his older brother Dwight (16.1 points and 9.9 rebounds per game) and future NBA player [[Clem Haskins]] (20.4 points and 10 rebounds per game).<ref name="College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Clem Haskins Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/haskicl01.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Western Kentucky won in the first round of the [[1966 NCAA University Division basketball tournament|1966 NCAA Men's Division I basketball tournament]], but lost the next game by one point (80–79) to the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|University of Michigan]] in the regional semifinals.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1966 NCAA tournament: Bracket, scores, stats, records {{!}} NCAA.com |url=https://www.ncaa.com/news/basketball-men/article/2020-05-13/1966-ncaa-tournament-bracket-scores-stats-records |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=www.ncaa.com |language=en}}</ref> Smith had nine points and 13 rebounds as a sophomore starter against Michigan.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Western Kentucky vs. Michigan Box Score (Men), March 11, 1966 |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/boxscores/1966-03-11-michigan.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

As a junior, he averaged 11.8 points and 10.9 rebounds per game. The [[1966–67 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers basketball team|1966–67 team]] was 23–3 and again won the Ohio Valley Conference championship, and they were ranked 6th in the final AP poll.<ref name="College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com-2">{{Cite web |title=1966–67 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Men's Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/western-kentucky/men/1967.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|University of Dayton]] eliminated the Hilltoppers 69–67 in overtime in the first round of the [[1967 NCAA University Division basketball tournament|1967 NCAA tournament]].<ref name="College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com-2"/> He, Haskins and Dwight Smith all averaged over 10 rebounds per game, with Greg Smith the 10th highest in the conference.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1966–67 Men's Ohio Valley Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/ovc/men/1967.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> As a senior, Smith averaged 13 points and 14.5 rebounds per game, but without Haskins and Dwight Smith, the 1967–68 Hilltoppers finished third in the Ohio Valley Conference in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1967–68 Western Kentucky Hilltoppers Men's Roster and Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/western-kentucky/men/1968.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Smith had the third highest rebounding average in the Ohio Valley Conference in 1968.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1967–68 Men's Ohio Valley Conference Leaders |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/conferences/ovc/men/1968.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Professional basketball ==
He was selected by the [[Kentucky Colonels]] in the [[American Basketball Association]]'s [[1968 ABA draft|1968 draft]],<ref>{{Cite news |date=May 6, 1968 |title=ABA Picks Leggett, Sapit |work=The Billings Gazette (Associated Press) |pages=14}}</ref> and by the Milwaukee Bucks in the fourth round of the [[1968 NBA draft]] (50th overall).<ref>{{Cite web |title=1968 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1968.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.basketballreference.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=SmithGr01 |title=BasketballReference.com Greg Smith page |access-date=2008-11-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071011102611/http://www.basketballreference.com/players/playerpage.htm?ilkid=SMITHGR01 |archive-date=2007-10-11 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Smith played forward for the Milwaukee Bucks (1968–71), [[Houston Rockets]] (1971–72) and [[Portland Trail Blazers]] (1972–75).

=== Milwaukee Bucks ===
Smith was a rookie on the expansion Milwaukee Buck's first team in 1968–69.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Historical Statistics and All-Time Top Leaders |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/ |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He played nearly 28 minutes per game, averaging 8.1 points and 10.2 rebounds per game. The team had a 27–55 record under rookie head coach [[Larry Costello]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1968–69 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/1969.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Larry Costello: Coaching Record, Awards |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/coaches/costela01c.html |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> The Bucks fortunes changed dramatically the following season after they drafted future Hall of Fame center, and one of the NBA's 75 greatest players ever, [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] (then generally known as Lew Alcindor) with the overall first pick in the [[1969 NBA draft]],<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-3">{{Cite web |title=1969 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1969.html |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Kareem Abdul-Jabbar |url=https://www.hoophall.com/hall-of-famers/kareem-abdul-jabbar/ |access-date=2025-07-01 |website=www.hoophall.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=NBA 75th Anniversary Team {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/nba-75-anniversary-team |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> and future NBA Hall of Fame forward  [[Bob Dandridge]] with their fourth-round pick.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-3" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Bob Dandridge |url=https://www.hoophall.com/hall-of-famers/bob-dandridge |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=www.hoophall.com |language=en}}</ref>

The 1969–70 Bucks improved by 29 games, with a regular season record of 56–26, finishing second in the Eastern division.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com">{{Cite web |title=1969–70 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/1970.html |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> They reached the Eastern Division Finals losing to the [[New York Knicks]] who would go on to win the [[1970 NBA playoffs|1970 NBA championship]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1970 NBA Eastern Division Finals – Bucks vs. Knicks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1970-nba-eastern-division-finals-bucks-vs-knicks.html |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1969–70 New York Knicks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/NYK/1970.html |access-date=2025-07-08 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Smith started at power forward, averaging 9.8 points and 8.7 rebounds in nearly 29 minutes per game.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com" /> He averaged a [[double-double]] (11.6 points, 10.6 rebounds) in the first round of the playoffs against the [[Philadelphia 76ers]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=1970 NBA Eastern Division Semifinals – 76ers vs. Bucks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1970-nba-eastern-division-semifinals-76ers-vs-bucks.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> and 9.8 points and 6.4 rebounds in the Knicks series.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1970 NBA Eastern Division Finals – Bucks vs. Knicks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1970-nba-eastern-division-finals-bucks-vs-knicks.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Smith helped the 66–16 Bucks win the [[1971 NBA Finals|1970–71 NBA Championship]].<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-4">{{Cite web |title=1970–71 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/1971.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In the 1970–71 season, Smith averaged 11.7 points, 7.2 rebounds and 2.8 assists per game.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-4"/> He averaged a double-double (11 points, 11.2 rebounds) in the first round playoff victory over the [[Golden State Warriors|San Francisco Warriors]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=1971 NBA Western Conference Semifinals – Bucks vs. Warriors |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1971-nba-western-conference-semifinals-bucks-vs-warriors.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 13.2 points, 6.2 rebounds and 3.2 assists in the five-game Western division finals win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]],<ref>{{Cite web |title=1971 NBA Western Conference Finals – Lakers vs. Bucks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1971-nba-western-conference-finals-lakers-vs-bucks.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> and 10 points and 8.3 rebounds per game in the NBA finals win over the [[Washington Wizards|Baltimore Bullets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1971 NBA Finals – Bullets vs. Bucks |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/playoffs/1971-nba-finals-bullets-vs-bucks.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Smith played only 28 games for the 1971–72 Bucks team that finished with a 63–19 record, winning the NBA Midwest Division. That team reached the Western division finals, losing to the Los Angeles Lakers two games to four.<ref>{{Cite web |title=1971–72 Milwaukee Bucks Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/MIL/1972.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> In early December 1971, the Bucks traded Smith and their third draft pick in the 1973 draft to the [[Houston Rockets]] for [[Curtis Perry]] and the Rockets first draft pick in the 1972 draft.<ref name="The Post-Crescent (Appleton, Wisconsin)-1971">{{Cite news |date=December 10, 1971 |title=Bucks' Greg Smith Dealt To Rockets for No. 1 pick |work=The Post-Crescent (Appleton, Wisconsin) |pages=26}}</ref>

The Bucks made the trade in the belief that they would be able to draft a talented and extremely valuable college player with the additional No. 1 draft pick.<ref name="The Post-Crescent (Appleton, Wisconsin)-1971" /> The Bucks used that pick (No. 6) to draft [[Russ Lee]], however, who played only two years for the Bucks and never averaged more than six minutes a game.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Russ Lee Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/l/leeru01.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=1972 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1972.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Perry finished out the 1971–72 season with the Bucks averaging seven points and 9.4 rebounds per game. He played two more years for the Bucks, averaging 9.1 points and 9.6 rebounds in 1972–73 and nine points and 8.7 rebounds in 1973–74.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Curtis Perry Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/p/perrycu01.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref>

Abdul-Jabbar considered Smith the key to the Bucks' championship team, and his absence from the team was one of the reasons they did not win another championship. Although only 6 ft, 5 in (1.96 m), small for a power forward, Smith could rebound well against much taller players and was as fast as any guard, making him a unique player to compete against. Abdul-Jabbar said that forwards like [[Gus Johnson (basketball)|Gus Johnson]] and [[Dave DeBusschere]] (both later in the Hall of Fame) hated playing against Smith.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-1982" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Gus Johnson |url=https://www.hoophall.com/hall-of-famers/gus-johnson/ |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=www.hoophall.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Dave DeBusschere |url=https://www.hoophall.com/hall-of-famers/dave-debusschere/ |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=www.hoophall.com |language=en}}</ref> Bucks teammate [[Oscar Robertson]] (another Hall of Famer and member of the 75th anniversary team)<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame :: Oscar Robertson |url=https://www.hoophall.com/hall-of-famers/oscar-robertson/ |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=www.hoophall.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Archive 75: Oscar Robertson {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/archive-75-oscar-robertson |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=NBA |language=en}}</ref> considered Smith the toughest defender he played against, when Robertson was on the [[Sacramento Kings|Cincinnati Royals]].<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" />

=== Houston Rockets and Portland Trail Blazers ===
Smith went from a first-place team in Milwaukee, to a Rockets team that finished 34–48 in the 1971–72 season.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-5">{{Cite web |title=1971–72 Houston Rockets Roster and Stats |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/teams/HOU/1972.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Smith averaged 2.9 assists per game with the Rockets, a career-high for any one team in a season, and 9.1 points; but only six rebounds per game.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-2" /><ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-5"/> The Rockets traded him early the next season to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] for [[Stan McKenzie (basketball)|Stan McKenzie]], on October 27, 1972.<ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/1972/10/28/archives/personalities-texas-gets-carry.html "Personalities: Texas Gets Carty," ''The New York Times'', Saturday, October 28, 1972.] Retrieved October 26, 2020</ref> He had been averaging just 10 minutes per game with the Rockets, and after the trade played about 22 minutes per game with the Trail Blazers to finish the 1972–73 season. Smith played the next two seasons as a reserve with the Trail Blazers, averaging 13.1 and 9.4 minutes per game respectively.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-2" /> Smith played only one game the following season before the Trail Blazers waived him in early November 1975, to activate rookie [[Lionel Hollins]].<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-2" /><ref>{{Cite news |date=November 8, 1975 |title=Basketball |work=The Sheboygan Press |pages=20}}</ref>

=== Career ===
In 8 seasons Smith played in 524 games and had 12,269 minutes played. He had a .482 field goal percentage (1,737 for 3,607), and a .646 free throw percentage (623 for 965). He recorded 3,249 total rebounds, 969 assists, 1,553 personal fouls and 4,097 points.<ref name="Basketball-Reference.com-2" />

== Personal life ==
In 1967, Smith's brother Dwight and sister Kay were killed in an automobile accident on a rainy night while driving with Smith, who survived in the submerged vehicle because he was in an air pocket.<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" /><ref name="Hutcheson-2023">{{Cite web |last=Hutcheson |first=Chip |date=2023-01-23 |title=WKU's Dwight Smith's legacy of basketball greatness lives on |url=https://www.pmg-ky1.com/the_anderson_news/wku-s-dwight-smiths-legacy-of-basketball-greatness-lives-on/article_5426040f-e489-5fec-a33d-adf203da2897.html |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=PMG-KY1.com |language=en}}</ref> Dwight had been selected by the Los Angeles Lakers in the third round of the [[1967 NBA draft]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=1967 NBA Draft |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/draft/NBA_1967.html |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He had averaged 14.6 points and 11 rebounds per game over his three-year career at Western Kentucky.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dwight Smith College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/dwight-smith-2.html |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> He was posthumously selected to Western Kentucky's Hall of Fame (1995), the Kentucky High School Basketball Hall of Fame (2016), the Ohio Valley Conference's 40th (1988) and 75th anniversary teams (2023), and Western Kentucky's All-Century basketball team (2018). Western Kentucky retired Dwight Smith's jersey number in 2023.<ref name="Hutcheson-2023" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=OVC 75th Anniversary Teams: Men's Basketball |url=http://ovcsports.com/news/2023/6/8/ovc-75th-anniversary-teams-mens-basketball.aspx |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=ovcsports.com |language=en}}</ref>

After retiring, Smith sold advertising for [[KGW (radio)|KGW radio]] in Portland, and also worked for Portland's exposition recreation commission.<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" /> He chaired the Oregon Black Republican Council from 1984 to 1988.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" /> Smith played [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball after retiring, and formed a Trail Blazers alumni team with some other retired players. For over two decades, the alumni team traveled around Oregon and parts of Washington, raising over $2 million for various non-profit organizations.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" />

Smith and his wife Linda have five children.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" /> His son Keith Smith was the 1985–86 Oregon high school basketball player of the year, and went on to play point guard on the [[California Golden Bears men's basketball|University of California]]'s basketball team (1986–90). He also played for the [[Albany Patroons]] in the [[Continental Basketball Association]].<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=Keith Smith College Stats |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/keith-smith-47.html |access-date=2025-07-17 |website=College Basketball at Sports-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref><ref name="Hutcheson-1991">{{Cite news |last=Hutcheson |first=Chip |date=April 10, 1991 |title=Greg Smith's son is football, track star; Atlanta writer says Ky. Sweet 16 the best |work=Times-Leader |pages=9}}</ref> He has a younger son, Damien Dwight Smith.<ref name="Engelhardt-1988" /> Damien was an athletic standout at Portland's [[Ida B. Wells-Barnett High School|Wilson High School]], excelling in basketball, football and track, despite two knee surgeries.<ref name="Hutcheson-1991" />

== Honors ==
Smith was inducted into the Kentucky High School Hall of Fame in 1997, and the Western Kentucky's Athletics Hall of Fame in 1998.<ref name="The Times-Ledger (Princeton, Kentucky)-2000" /><ref>{{Cite web |title=WKU Athletic Hall of Fame |url=https://wkusports.com/sports/2017/6/8/ot-hall-of-fame-2-html |access-date=2025-07-18 |website=Western Kentucky University Athletics |language=en}}</ref> He was inducted into the Kentucky High School Basketball Hall of Fame in 2023, with him and Dwight being the only brothers in this hall of fame.<ref name="Kentucky High School Basketball Hall Of Fame-2023" />
